# apple_app_encryption_declaration_document (Resource)

Uploads the export compliance documentation of an encryption declaration, such as a French encryption declaration or a CCATS. A declaration has one document; uploading another replaces it. A changed file is uploaded as a new one, which replaces the resource. App Store Connect can't delete it, so destroying the resource leaves it. Import it by ID; the next apply then uploads the configured file.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "apple_app_encryption_declaration_document" "ccats" {
  declaration_id = apple_app_encryption_declaration.example.id
  file           = "${path.module}/compliance/ccats.pdf"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `declaration_id` (String) App Store Connect ID of the encryption declaration, e.g. `apple_app_encryption_declaration.example.id`.
- `file` (String) Path of the file to upload. Relative paths are relative to where Terraform runs, so use `"${path.module}/..."`.

### Read-Only

- `checksum` (String) MD5 checksum of the file.
- `id` (String) App Store Connect ID of the encryption declaration document.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = apple_app_encryption_declaration_document.ccats
  identity = {
    id = "1234567890"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) App Store Connect ID of the encryption declaration document.

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import apple_app_encryption_declaration_document.ccats 1234567890
```
